taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Historical confusion with Fraxinus pennsylvanica and F. velutina makes reproductive and leaflet characters especially important.
look_here_first: Count the leaflets and inspect a samara. Mexican ash usually has 3–5 leaflets with coarse sharp serration toward the tips; samara wings expand gradually from near the base, and occasional 3-winged fruits can occur.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Later manual reconciliation retained Travis and Comal and added Bexar from a voucher-backed San Antonio Missions flora.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Because this ash has a history of confusion with green and velvet ash, do not infer county presence from ambiguous Fraxinus records.

best_field_traits: leaflet margins coarsely and sharply serrate on distal half to two-thirds
lower leaflet surface glabrous in the Central Texas comparison treatment
leaf scar shallowly hemispheric with shallowly concave apex
samaras usually 2-winged but occasional 3-winged fruits may occur
samara wings gradually expand from near the base and narrowly flange the fruit body
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Green ash generally carries more leaflets and has a broader shield-shaped scar with differently broadened samaras; Texas ash tends to have 5–7 leaflets, a glaucous lower surface, and smaller mostly terminal-winged samaras.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use leaflet count/serration, lower leaflet surface, leaf scar, and especially samara structure together; occasional 3-winged fruits are a useful supporting clue.
